records.title: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme — Cycle 2026
records.summary: Botswana nationals can seek one of 10 UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi fellowships—up to US$10,000—for a 3–9 month research stay in Japan from February 2027 in heritage conservation, sustainable development or AI-related areas.
records.body_markdown:
## Overview

Botswana nationals can seek one of 10 UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi fellowships—up to US$10,000—for a 3–9 month research stay in Japan from February 2027 in heritage conservation, sustainable development or AI-related areas.

## Location

Japan (research stay; open to Botswana nationals)

## Requirements

- Be a national of an invited state; Botswana is listed
- Be no more than 40 years old at application
- Hold at least a master's degree or equivalent relevant to the proposed research
- Demonstrate strong academic and research potential
- Have sufficient reading and writing proficiency in the host institution's language of instruction or supervision
- Secure acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution
- Submit a proposal in an eligible 2026 research area

## How to apply

Read UNESCO's application guide, prepare the application form and supporting documents, and submit them first to the Botswana National Commission for UNESCO for nomination. Only National Commission-nominated applications are accepted by UNESCO.

## Closing date

2026-10-15 (midnight Paris time)

## Official source

[UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers’ Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme)](https://www.unesco.org/en/fellowships/keizo-obuchi)
